source.name: 4Chan Threads Text Archive Ten Billion 2009
source.short-desc: A text-only compilation of roughly 10 million unique 4chan threads, primarily 2006-2008, from an anonymous donor. Uploaded to the Internet Archive by Jason Scott in October 2018 under the archiveteam collection. The item ships the same corpus three times over: HTML, XML and MySQL.
source.capture: 22GB across three renderings of one corpus, and only the XML is ingestible. threads/xml/<board>.tar.gz (4.5GB, 42 boards) is one <thread> file per thread: <link> giving host+board+OP number, then nested <post num= date=> with optional <poster>, <tripcode>, <email>, <subject>, <text> CDATA and <img/> (always empty — this is the text-only dump). threads/style/fourchan.xsl is the stylesheet that rendered it and documents the full field set. threads/html/<board>.tar.gz (7.1GB, 44 boards) is that XML run through the XSL with the number and date templates producing NOTHING: every post is just postername + blockquote, so replies carry no post_no at all and no post carries a timestamp. It is kept only for /b/ (3.3GB) and /p/, the two boards the XML tree omits, where the OP number is still recoverable from the filename; the other 42 HTML boards are excluded as redundant. chanarchive.tar.gz (10.5GB) is the MySQL form, but as raw MyISAM table files (chanarchive/threads.MYD, ...), not a mysqldump — reading it means attaching the tables to a MySQL server, so no existing adapter touches it. It is downloaded anyway because it is the only candidate holding /b/ WITH post numbers. XML dates are minute precision with no seconds and no timezone ('2006-09-16 23:23'); they are presumably 4chan's displayed New-York wall time and would need nyWallToUtc like fybertech, but that is UNVERIFIED — cross-check a shared post against another archive before trusting it.

prepare.name: unpack the per-board XML tarballs
prepare.run: mkdir -p extracted/xml && for f in source/threads/xml/*.tar.gz; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; b=$(basename "$f" .tar.gz); [ -d "extracted/xml/$b" ] || tar xzf "$f" -C extracted/xml; done

prepare.name: unpack the /b/ and /p/ HTML tarballs (the boards the XML tree omits)
prepare.run: mkdir -p extracted/html && for b in b p; do f="source/threads/html/$b.tar.gz"; [ -e "$f" ] || continue; [ -d "extracted/html/$b" ] || tar xzf "$f" -C extracted/html; done

prepare.name: stage for ingest
prepare.run: rm -rf out && (cp -al extracted out 2>/dev/null || cp -a extracted out)
